assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Elastic potential energy (Ee)
items.clue: What a stretched or squashed spring stores.

items.label: Extension (e)
items.clue: The stretched length minus the original length.

items.label: Kinetic energy (Ek)
items.clue: What a moving object stores because of its motion.

items.label: Gravitational field strength (g)
items.clue: The force acting on each kilogram of mass, in N/kg.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 500 g is moving at a speed of 6 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A toy car of mass 0.8 kg is moving at a speed of 5 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A van doubles its speed. Its mass does not change. What happens to its kinetic energy?

options.text: it grows in the same ratio as the speed
it becomes four times as large as before
it becomes twice as large as before
it stays the same size as before

questions.explanation: Speed is squared in E_k = 1/2 m v^2, so a factor of 2 on the speed gives a factor of 2^2 = 4 on the energy.

questions.stem: Which of these is the equation E_k = 1/2 m v^2 written out in words?
questions.explanation: This is the equation as the specification states it: the speed, and only the speed, is squared.

questions.stem: A kinetic energy calculation uses a mass in kilograms and a speed in metres per second. The answer is in which unit?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy, like every energy store in this section, is measured in joules, J.

questions.stem: A student puts the mass of a 250 g ball straight into E_k = 1/2 m v^2 as 250. Why is the answer wrong?

options.text: the speed should not have been squared
the mass has to be in newtons, so m should be 2.5
the answer is right, but the unit is newtons
the mass has to be in kilograms, so m should be 0.25

questions.explanation: The equation needs the mass in kilograms, and 250 g = 250/1000 = 0.25 kg.

questions.stem: A car's speed is given as 72 km/h. What must be done before using E_k = 1/2 m v^2?

options.text: convert the speed to metres per second
convert the speed into kilometres per minute
use 72 as the speed and convert the answer
square 72 first and then halve the answer

questions.explanation: The equation requires the speed v in m/s, so 72 km/h must be converted to 20 m/s first.

questions.stem: Which pair of quantities is needed to calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object?

options.text: the force applied and the speed reached
the weight and the speed of the object
the mass and the speed of the object
the mass and the distance travelled

questions.explanation: E_k = 1/2 m v^2 contains only the mass and the speed; nothing else about the object is needed.

questions.stem: A spring has a spring constant of 200 N/m. It is stretched, within its limit of proportionality, so that its extension is 0.1 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored in the spring?
A spring with a spring constant of 400 N/m is stretched by an extension of 5 cm, staying within its limit of proportionality. How much elastic potential energy is stored?
The energy stored in a stretched spring is E_e = 1/2 k e^2. What do the symbols k and e stand for?

options.text: the spring constant and the energy of the spring
the spring constant and the force applied to it
the spring constant and the stretched length
the spring constant and the extension of the spring

questions.explanation: k is the spring constant, in N/m, and e is the extension, in m.

questions.stem: A spring is stretched within its limit of proportionality. The elastic potential energy stored in it is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy, like every energy store, is measured in joules, J.
